household.name: plaque; comb
household.title: plaque; comb
household.reason: An intricately carved ivory comb/plaque with kinnaras (mythical bird-women) holding vinas amid foliage scrollwork — a classic Sinhalese ivory-carving motif, consistent with the museum's attribution.

garment.name: dance-skirt
garment.title: dance-skirt
garment.reason: This is a red cotton dance skirt with black-and-white zigzag piping and green accents, identified as a devil dancer's (Tovil) costume made by Sinhalese performers — a traditional Sri Lankan ritual garment.

garment.name: paraphernalia, dance run, dress
garment.title: paraphernalia, dance run, dress
garment.reason: A hemp/yarn fringed apron worn by Sinhalese demon-ceremony (yak tovil) dancers, dyed with kukul sayam paint — a documented traditional Sinhalese ritual dance garment.

garment.name: dance-skirt
garment.title: dance-skirt
garment.reason: A cotton tovil (devil-dancing) skirt with red/white sections and piped braid decoration, attributed by the museum to Sinhalese make — this is a known traditional ritual dance costume element from Sri Lanka.

arms.name: knife
arms.title: knife
arms.reason: This is a pihiya, a traditional Sinhalese knife with a carved/engraved brass bolster and handle fittings typical of Kandyan metalwork, consistent with Sri Lankan craft traditions.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: An ivory figure of a standing Kandyan provincial governor (disave), with characteristic conical hat, sarong, and belt, attributed to Sinhalese makers — a known Kandyan-era ivory carving tradition.

sculpture.name: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.title: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden puppet head with crown headdress representing a minister (ämati), used in Sri Lankan Sinhalese string puppetry (nul rukadaya) — a traditional craft and performance object of this culture.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: An ivory carving of a standing woman in elaborate court dress with jewellery, labeled as the wife of a disave (provincial governor), with the museum crediting Sinhalese production — a well-attested genre of Kandyan-era Sinhalese ivory carving.

sculpture.name: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.title: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.reason: The carved wooden puppet head represents a prince (kumara) and is part of the Sinhalese string-puppet (nul rukadaya) tradition from Sri Lanka, a documented craft of the Sinhalese people.

sculpture.name: figure
sculpture.title: figure
sculpture.reason: A small bronze standing female deity figure (probably Tara) in tribhanga pose with kataka mudra — a classic Sinhalese Buddhist bronze type, consistent with the museum's attribution.

sculpture.name: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.title: figur, docka, puppet
sculpture.reason: This is a painted wooden string-puppet head representing a Sinhalese king (raja), used in Sri Lankan nul rukadaya puppet theatre — a clear example of Sinhalese traditional craft and performance culture.

photo.name: Studioportret van een Sinhalese vrouw, Ceylon
photo.title: Studioportret van een Sinhalese vrouw, Ceylon
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Sinhalese woman in traditional Kandyan-style dress with layered bead necklaces, bangles, and a patterned osari cloth, matching the claimed ethnicity and documentary photo category.

photo.name: Sinhalese dwellings
photo.title: Sinhalese dwellings
photo.reason: The photo shows a group of Sinhalese villagers in front of thatched-roof houses with a shop stall displaying bananas and goods, documenting traditional dwelling and daily life in Ceylon, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.title: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: Studio photograph of a Sinhalese man identified as a government peon (messenger/official attendant) in Ceylon, wearing traditional comb-and-topknot hair ornament and local dress elements with a Western-style jacket, documenting Sinhalese dress/occupation of the period.

photo.name: photographic print; album; postcard
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album; postcard
photo.reason: Documentary postcard photo of a group of low-country Sinhalese women and a child in Colombo, wearing traditional cloth wraps outdoors; a straightforward ethnographic record of dress and daily life.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black & white); album
photo.reason: A documentary photo of a Sinhalese woman holding a child outside a tiled-roof house in Colombo, showing traditional dress and daily life, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.title: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: Studio/documentary photo of a Sinhalese woman in Ceylon wearing a plaid wrapped skirt and blouse with jewelry, captioned "Sinhalese Woman, Ceylon" by period photographer Skeen; matches the claimed ethnicity and category.

photo.name: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.title: porträtt, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: Studio portrait of a Sinhalese toddy drawer (coconut palm tapper) from Ceylon, shown with his waist cloth, toddy pots, and climbing tools used in his traditional occupation — a documentary type photo by the Skeen studio of Sri Lanka.

instruments.name: klocka, bell
instruments.title: klocka, bell
instruments.reason: A bronze temple bell (ghantaraya) with wooden handle, documented as used by Sinhalese (and Hindus) in Sri Lankan temples — a plausible traditional Sinhalese ritual/instrument object.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A tall painted wooden Kolam headdress-mask depicting King Maha Sammata, a figure from the Sinhalese Kolam masked dance tradition of Sri Lanka, with crown and elaborate tiered ornamentation typical of this genre.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved and painted wooden riri yaka demon mask with cobra-hood headdress, used in Sinhalese exorcism/healing ceremonies (Rata Yakuma) — a classic Sinhalese ritual object.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: This is a carved and painted Kolam ritual mask from Sri Lanka (identified as a king/Väda chief character), a classic Sinhalese dance-drama mask with elaborate crown, large ears, and polychrome decoration — fully consistent with Sinhalese ritual/theatre tradition.

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden Kolam ritual mask depicting a vädi kumari character, a traditional Sinhalese dance-drama mask with typical headdress and dark-green/black face paint — a classic Sinhalese ritual mask type.
